goal: Validate the Doomstack layout + jitter/UX change set (branch claude/blissful-ramanujan-tcniuq, d5bb5e3..HEAD) against AC-1..AC-29 end-to-end, with dedicated browser validation of the three interaction/viewport ACs the verifier flagged (AC-9, AC-19, AC-27) and an assessment of the reviewer's non-blocking handleFindMe rAF warning.
summary: All 29 acceptance criteria pass. I drove real Chromium (Playwright, /opt/pw-browsers, --no-sandbox, reduced-motion emulated) against the live dev app. AC-27: zero horizontal overflow on all four pages at 375px; every in-scope flow control is >=44px; the only sub-44 controls are the out-of-scope navbar (38-40px) / footer (36px) and inline prose links (WCAG inline exception) - no regression introduced by this change set. AC-9: validated with real browser evidence - I seeded Firebase's IndexedDB with a non-expired user (no code change) so onIdTokenChanged signs in the real DuelHome, then intercepted /api/duel/queue to hold 'searching'; the matchmaking bar rendered with a spinner + Cancel search, and the elapsed readout ticked 0:00->0:01->0:02->0:03->0:04 at exactly 1 Hz; Cancel removed the bar AND issued DELETE /api/duel/queue. AC-19: the full end-to-end path is NOT reachable in this sandbox (the /climb standings are server-rendered from Prisma and there is no DB, so no rows render and the 'Find me' button never mounts) - validated by inspection instead; the mechanism is sound (row carries id=your-climb-row + scroll-mt-20, highlight always applied, query cleared before scroll) and the reviewer's single-rAF warning is non-blocking (React 18 flushes the discrete click update synchronously before the scheduled rAF fires, so the re-mounted row is committed when scrollIntoView runs; worst case the row is still highlighted and visible). Using the same auth mock I additionally confirmed the signed-in ACs that the sandbox otherwise hides: AC-16 (panel shows 1234ft / #5 / 99 climbers from /api/dashboard), AC-17 (dashboard 500 -> CTA-only fallback, single /play CTA, table unaffected), AC-11 (record strip '7W 2L +3streak'), AC-7 (Quick Match + Challenge a friend in md:grid-cols-2). Degrade states verified as the expected graceful paths (no DB): /climb shows the 'standings unavailable' ember state (never 'no climbers yet'), hub stat strip shows dash. Verifier already confirmed 794 tests + lint + typecheck green (AC-29). No acceptance failure; two non-blocking cosmetic notes recorded. Proceed to integrator. Working tree clean; dev server stopped; throwaway Playwright scripts live only in the session scratchpad.

exitCriteria.flagged_interaction_viewport_acs_validat: AC-9 real-browser tick confirmed; AC-27 real-browser overflow+targets confirmed; AC-19 mechanism inspected (server-standings path blocked by no-DB sandbox)

nonBlockingNotes: ClimbBoard.handleFindMe uses a single requestAnimationFrame after setQuery('') (ClimbBoard.tsx:116-124). Sound in React 18 for the discrete click path, but fragile as the reviewer noted; a double-rAF or an effect keyed on the row's presence would be more robust. Cosmetic - do not block.

Daily streak strip: an UNPLAYED current day renders sr-only text 'Saturday - missed' (DailyClimbClient.tsx:280-287) because the else-branch labels non-future non-played days 'missed'. For *today* specifically 'not yet' (or 'today, not climbed') would read better. Cosmetic a11y wording, not an AC failure.
sandboxLimitations: No database: /climb server-rendered standings (topFreeClimbers) return null, so the board shows the AC-20 'standings unavailable' degrade and no rows render. This makes AC-18 (filter over rows) and AC-19 (Find me scroll) un-exercisable end-to-end in the browser; both validated by code inspection + unit smoke tests.
No automated gameplay: AC-23's daily result panel requires a finished ClimbScene run (canvas); validated by code inspection.

No real Firebase session: signed-in ACs (AC-7/9/11/16/17) were validated by seeding Firebase IndexedDB with a non-expired user and stubbing the Google identity + relevant /api endpoints via Playwright route interception - this exercises the REAL production components/hooks, not re-implementations.

learnings.insight: Auth-gated flows (Firebase onIdTokenChanged) can be exercised in a real browser without a live session: Playwright addInitScript to seed IndexedDB 'firebaseLocalStorageDb' store 'firebaseLocalStorage' with { fbase_key: `firebase:authUser:<apiKey>:[DEFAULT]`, value: <UserImpl with stsTokenManager.expirationTime in the future> }, plus route.fulfill stubs for identitytoolkit.googleapis.com (accounts:lookup) and securetoken.googleapis.com (token). A future expirationTime makes getIdToken() return the cached token with no network. This drives the ACTUAL production component (real useElapsedSeconds tick verified 0:00->0:04 at 1 Hz), so it is not a re-implementation. This was the only way to validate AC-9/AC-11/AC-16/AC-17 in this no-DB/no-auth sandbox.
learnings.action: Reuse this seed+stub recipe to browser-validate any Firebase-auth-gated UI when no real login is available.

learnings.insight: AC-18 and AC-19 both operate over the /climb standings, which are a SERVER prop (topFreeClimbers via Prisma). In a no-DB sandbox the board renders the 'standings unavailable' degrade with zero rows, so the search filter and the 'Find me' button never appear - these ACs cannot be browser-exercised without a DB or a seeded fixture. Their correctness rests on code inspection + the climbBoardSmoke/climbBoardViewerPanel unit tests.
learnings.action: If AC-19's scroll robustness ever matters in production, harden handleFindMe (double-rAF or presence-keyed effect) and add a component test that mounts ClimbBoard with fixture climbers so the interaction is actually covered.

learnings.insight: All 29 ACs pass; AC-9 (1 Hz timer + cancel/DELETE) and AC-27 (375px, no overflow, in-scope targets >=44px) confirmed with real-browser evidence; AC-19 mechanism sound with the reviewer's rAF warning assessed non-blocking. Two cosmetic non-blocking notes only. Working tree clean, dev server stopped.
learnings.action: Safe to integrate; carry the two cosmetic notes as follow-ups, not blockers.
